name: Czechia
tagline: Your IB skips the paperwork everyone else has to do
summary: Since 1 March 2025 Czech law accepts the IB Diploma directly, with no nostrification. Study in Czech is free for everyone; English-taught degrees charge fees set by each university. There is no central portal: you apply faculty by faculty, and some deadlines fall after IB results.
whyConsider: The IB is accepted by law without nostrification.
Many English-taught programmes, including medicine, at moderate fees and low living costs.
Some faculties close after IB results, so you can apply on real grades.
watchOuts: Every faculty has its own application, fee, exam and deadline.
Most 2027 deadlines were not yet published in September 2026.
Older pages may still say the IB needs nostrification; the law changed on 1 March 2025.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: None nationally. Faculties set their own subject requirements, notably for medicine.
notes: Section 48(4)(c) of Act No. 111/1998 Coll., in force since 1 March 2025, accepts the IB Diploma as proof of completed secondary education.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Wide, concentrated at the large public universities and in medicine.

feeContext.summary: Programmes taught in Czech at public universities are free, whatever your nationality.
English-taught programmes charge fees set by each university, from a few hundred euros a year to over 20,000 for medicine. Some charge EU citizens less.

sectorLandscape.summary: Czech higher education institutions (vysoké školy) are either university-type (univerzitní) or non-university-type (neuniverzitní), and public, state or private. Below them sit the vyšší odborné školy, tertiary professional schools outside the Higher Education Act.

routes.what: Charles, Masaryk, CTU and the other public universities: bachelor's, master's and doctorates, with English-taught programmes in many faculties, especially medicine, engineering and business.
Institutions offering bachelor's and master's but not doctorates, many of them private and several teaching in English, such as Anglo-American University.
Three-year practical programmes under the Education Act rather than the Higher Education Act, ending in a diploma rather than a degree.
routes.note: Not researched here; almost certainly taught in Czech.

notes: The IB clause, § 48(4)(c), was read in the Czech original on 2026-09-24. §§ 2 and 58 were read only through a fetch tool that paraphrased them; a person should read them in Czech.
The vyšší odborná škola description comes from a Czech ministry search result, not a page that could be opened; msmt.gov.cz pages returned 'page not found' on 2026-09-23.
